purpose: Teach: キャサリン/永田町/シェリー/ビクター/ディーン/クラッチ/ハンス/マルタ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがキャサリン女王の特集番組を観られた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he used to watch documentaries about Queen Catherine.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle curiosity in the voice—asking her to remember with him. Unhurried pace, almost conversational musing. Let the memory settle in the space between you.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、永田町に通うお仕事だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear—your father worked in Nagatacho back then, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, affirming tone. Small smile underneath the words. Patient, as if gently guiding him through a familiar path. Speak with the ease of someone who's held these memories a long time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがスペインのシェリー酒を取り寄せた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he had Spanish sherry specially ordered for him.
lines.style: Same wistful tone as before, but with a touch more wonder—the luxury of it. Deliberate, almost reverential. Let each detail land gently, like placing an old photograph on the table.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ビクターのレコードプレーヤーをお持ちだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father had a Victor record player, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Connecting the threads. Warm, slightly teasing affection in 'dear.' She's offering him another piece, another shared memory. Steady, knowing tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがジェームス・ディーンに憧れたんだって
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he admired James Dean.
lines.style: The wistfulness deepens slightly—there's boyishness in this memory. Slower pace here, lingering on the name. Quiet recognition of youthful longing across the years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、車のクラッチ操作が上手だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your father was quite skilled at working the car clutch, wasn't he?
lines.style: Light, almost teasing affection now. She's building a portrait of him as he was—capable, modern, alive. Speak with gentle pride, the warmth of someone who knew him in his prime.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがハンス・クリスチャン・アンデルセンの童話を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he read Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales.
lines.style: A softer, more intimate memory. Slower still. Almost a whisper to himself. The literary detail adds a quieter weight. Let the tenderness of a young man reading fairy tales show in your voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、マルタ島へ新婚旅行に行ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you two took a honeymoon trip to Malta, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: This is the closing memory, and it lands differently—not about his father now, but about them. Warmth blooms. Slight catch of affection in her voice. She's bringing him home to their own story. Softer fade at the end.
